content.title: NEW PARENTS: DO THESE 7 THINGS BEFORE YOU EVEN THINK ABOUT SLEEP TRAINING
facts: **Eat standing up if you have to** – but get 20g of protein in before noon, it keeps your blood sugar from crashing into a 3pm meltdown.
**Drink 1 glass of water** before every feed/pump session, not after - dehydration sneaks up fast when you're running on broken sleep.
**Step outside for 5 minutes** within an hour of waking, morning light resets your body clock even if your schedule is total chaos.
**Batch snacks you don't have to think about** - string cheese, boiled eggs, trail mix - decision fatigue is real and it's not about willpower.
**Set a 2-minute timer for deep breathing** when the crying hits a wall, it won't fix the moment but it lowers your cortisol enough to think clearly.
**Ask one person for one specific task** this week, not 'let me know if you need anything' - specific requests actually get answered.
**Lie down even if you can't sleep** during one nap a day, rest without sleep still lowers physical stress on your body.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
The protein push matters more than people admit - when you're sleep-deprived, your blood sugar swings harder and faster, and low protein in the morning makes that 3pm crash brutal. Water timing is another sneaky one: new parents chronically under-drink because thirst cues get buried under everything else happening, and mild dehydration alone can mimic fatigue and irritability. And that 5-minute morning light habit isn't just a nice idea - natural light exposure early in the day helps anchor your circadian rhythm even when your actual sleep schedule is fragmented and unpredictable. Everyone's body and situation is different, so take what fits your week.
